cells.tense: You are here, at the point where what matters shows up before you can explain why.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing that has been quietly holding your direction and say out loud what it is for. Let the sitting-still be part of the pace for a day.
cells.core:
You are at the point where what matters shows up before you can explain why, and you move on it. The direction holds through resistance without eating you. You do not need the whole argument in place to know that something is worth going toward, and not being sure yet does not stall you. It's a calm kind of traction.

That ease has a cost to keep. The read is quiet enough that you can start treating it as mood and stop naming what you're going by. When you name it, the momentum gets sturdier, because the choice carries your name on it. When you don't, you still move, but the direction floats a little. So put one sentence around what you're already following, and let one thing be chosen out loud today.
cells.sheetLine: You know what matters before you can say why, and you move on it.
cells.verb: seeing what matters before you can say how you know

cells.tense: You are outrunning the point where you recognize what matters, racing a future that has not been written yet.
cells.ask: Take one question you have been trying to get certain about and act on it while it is still open, then stop gathering for the day.
cells.core:
You are racing a future that has not been written yet. There is a version out there where you will have enough information to be sure, and you are living in it already — so every pause becomes another round of collecting, comparing, checking. The direction you wanted gets buried under the checking. Recognizing what matters starts to look like proof instead of recognition.

What happens when the gathering stops, even for an afternoon? The pull that was pointing at something goes unheard because there is no room left for it to arrive. You might doubt the draw toward what is genuinely wanted and call it a distraction from the task. Let the unfinished question stay unfinished today and see if the direction still shows through. You may find the aim was already clear, just crowded out.
cells.sheetLine: The gathering has replaced the recognition it was supposed to serve.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that is already behind you, still waiting for it to open.
cells.ask: Take one thing you already sense is right and make it real this week without asking anyone whether it is right first.
cells.core:
Nothing you notice feels like it can be trusted on its own, so everything goes out for a second opinion before it counts. The motive force that used to take you somewhere is emptied out, and you keep hunting for a stamp on what you see.

What is missing is not more input. It is the sense that one perception belongs to you. There may be a way through the uncertainty here: a small imaginative step that doesn't force the whole picture into focus. Try walking one thing you sense without clearing it first. The direction is still there; you just stopped letting it drive.
cells.sheetLine: Your own read keeps getting sent out for approval before it counts.

cells.tense: You are already writing this in a room where the pen is still down.
cells.ask: Name one choice you have been calling random and say which of your own perceptions pushed it that way.
cells.core:
The decisions you describe as arbitrary keep landing in places that fit something you had noticed earlier and didn't count at the time. Some part of the read was accurate. The navigation happened before the explanation, and you keep giving the credit to timing.

The awkwardness is not that you don't know. It's that the read keeps surprising the person doing it. If anything, that is a sign the direction is being steered by something you haven't signed for yet. You might be discounting the sense that made the call as random or lucky. Put your name on one choice today and see whether the aim feels more like it belongs to you.
cells.sheetLine: You decided something real and called it a coincidence.
